t: A tiny, very cheap RISC-V chip with Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, and Zigbee radios.
steps: Buy a board such as the Ai-Thinker Ai-M61-32S kit from RobotShop or a Sipeed M0S Dock from AliExpress.
Download the free Bouffalo SDK from its GitHub page.
Install the RISC-V GCC toolchain that the SDK README names.
Install the open bflb-mcu-tool flasher with Python.
Build the blink example from the SDK examples folder.
Hold the BOOT button and plug in the USB-C cable. Then flash the example.
Try the Wi-Fi example next and join your home network.
meta: Open Board. From $4.39. A few stores.
